clauses.text:
By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in me by the Career Com­
pensation Act of 1949, approved October 
12,1949 (Public Law 351, 81st Congress), 
Executive Order No. 10084 of October 12, 
1949, entitled “Prescribing Regulations 
for the Administration of Certain Provi­
sions of the Career Compensation Act of 
1949”, as amended by Executive Orders 
No. 10098 of January 25, 1950, No. 10118 
of March 27,1950, and No. 10136 of June 
30, 1950, is hereby further amended as 
follows :
.1 . To the extent that such order adopts 
and prescribes regulations required or 
authorized to be prescribed by the Presi­
dent under sections 206 and 302 of the 
Career Compensation Act of 1949, it shall 
continue in effect until October 31, 1950.
This order shall become effective on 
September 1' 1950.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 10158 (15 FR 5927 (Federal Register of September 1, 1950)) concerns the order that adopts, as regulations under Titles II, III and V of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, the existing pay regulations, and fixes how long that adoption lasts. Executive Order 10158 was signed August 31, 1950 and becomes effective September 1, 1950. Its only command amends Executive Order No. 10084 (as amended by Executive Orders No. 10098, No. 10118 and No. 10136) so that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 206 and 302 of the Act, it continues in effect until October 31, 1950. Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Each amendment takes effect the day after the earlier date it extends ends, so the dates are read inclusively and leave no gap. The last held instrument is Executive Order 10174 (15 FR 7165 (Federal Register of October 26, 1950)), which continues the order, to the extent it adopts regulations under section 302 of the Act, “until January 31, 1951”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated at that last sunset, January 31, 1951, inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins. The dossier's later-event chain and the held-text search for citations of Executive Order No. 10084 (searched also with a trailing footnote digit) show no later instrument after Executive Order 10174: the Federal Register disposition-note search lists the five amendments named above, and the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit. A later extension that the held corpus lacks is not excluded, which is the usual limit of a bounded search and is disclosed.
